record.paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
record.original_question: For the critically loaded finite-capacity queue GI/G/1/K with arrival rate λ equal to service rate μ, renewal inter-arrival process with squared coefficient of variation c_a^2, i.i.d. service times with squared coefficient of variation c_s^2, and K finite buffer capacity, does the BRAVO effect hold in the sense that the long-run departure-process variability parameter γ* satisfies γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) as K grows, at least for light-tailed inter-arrival and service-time distributions? Equivalently, is the large-K critical-load analogue of the known GI/G/1 and M/M/1/K formulas given by the factor 1/3 multiplying c_a^2 + c_s^2?

evidence.quote: A missing piece in the puzzle is the GI/G/1/K queue: Is there a BRAVO effect? If so, what is the variability? Does 1/3 play a role?
Conjecture 1 For the GI/G/1/K queue with λ = μ and light-tailed inter-arrival and service times, γ∗ = 1/3 (c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite buffer capacity K (so the system holds at most K customers including the one in service; arriving customers finding the buffer full are lost). Inter-arrival times form a renewal process with rate λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2, and service times are i.i.d., independent of arrivals, with rate μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. Assume the critical loading λ = μ and that both inter-arrival and service-time distributions are light-tailed (e.g., have all exponential moments finite in a neighborhood of 0).

Let D(t) denote the number of customers that have departed (completed service) by time t, and define the asymptotic variability parameter of the departure process by
   γ* := lim_{t→∞} Var(D(t)) / E[D(t)],
assuming this limit exists.

Prove or disprove the following: as K → ∞,
   γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).

That is, establish whether the BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Outputs) phenomenon, known to hold with factor 1/3 in the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 critical case and in the M/M/1/K critical case, extends to the general critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue under light-tailed assumptions, with the indicated O(1/K) correction.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. Subsequent work has settled BRAVO for the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 critical queue and for many-server QED systems with finite buffers, and the M/M/1/K case is known explicitly, but no published result establishes the (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) formula for the general critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue with light-tailed inter-arrival and service distributions.

status_evidence.title: On busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and BRAVO
status_evidence.snippet: Settles previously conjectured GI/G/1 and GI/G/s BRAVO results (infinite buffer).
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress settled the infinite-buffer GI/G/1 BRAVO, but did not address GI/G/1/K.

status_evidence.title: BRAVO for Many-Server QED Systems with Finite Buffers
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes BRAVO for many-server QED systems with finite buffers.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-buffer BRAVO addressed in many-server QED regime, not in single-server GI/G/1/K.

status_evidence.title: Phase transitions and departure statistics of critically loaded queues
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses BRAVO effect in M/M/1/K and generalizations but does not prove the GI/G/1/K conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work generalizes BRAVO observations but does not resolve the GI/G/1/K conjecture.
